decision.about: How many rungs belong under --gap in the size standard?

options.say: Five rungs — the gap plus four
options.why: What the existing code already supports: 390 of 470 multipliers land within 15% of a rung, 83%.
Fewer names to learn, and no readable set of four reaches 80% — the best is 79.6%.
The stricter design, and it moves about 70% of scaled values by more than 15%.
A middle that was never fitted to the census, so its coverage is unknown.

decision.because: Five is what the code already does at 83% coverage; two is the better design but moves 70% of the site, which is the owner's call to make, not a build's.

decision.about: Where should the layout browser live?

options.why: Beside the encyclopedia it indexes — the reader judging a layout is already there.
With the other review tools, away from the corpus it judges.

decision.because: The browser is a view OF the encyclopedia, and a review tool nobody passes on their way anywhere is a tool nobody opens.

decision.about: At 3440, should the Reader practice layout centre its article or span the screen?

options.say: Centre the article and accept the gutter
options.why: Holds the measure; 1,860px of grey sat between the article and its own notes.

options.say: Give a region the leftover to spend
options.why: Uses the screen the owner asked us to use — and needs a region with content worth the room.

decision.because: Both pass every numeric check, and which one is right is a taste call about what a wide screen is FOR.

decision.about: Which of three nav tunings goes into core's Page.css?

options.say: A ceiling on the nav track
options.why: Stops it growing, and leaves 3440 with an unfilled band.

options.say: A floor on the nav track
options.why: Keeps it usable narrow, and does nothing about the wide end.
Holds still across widths AND fills 3440 — the recommendation in the return report.

decision.because: It is the only one of the three that is both stable across widths and fills the wide screen; the lab shows the difference and the core declaration is NOT applied until the owner rules.

decision.about: Apply the core children-as-data-source change, or hold it as a proposal?

options.say: Apply it, flagged as one revert away
options.why: The owner's page-as-data sentence asked for it, and a proposal nobody can click is not a demonstration.

options.say: Leave it as a written proposal
options.why: Zero risk to the one file every page in the site runs through.

decision.because: It is the one core change of the run, made on the owner's own sentence, and it is one revert away with the revert named in the report.

decision.about: Should even columns be a core mode, or a page-level arrangement?

options.why: Every columns host gets it for free and there is one implementation to fix.

options.say: An arrangement each page opts into
options.why: Core stays smaller, and every page that wants it copies the same sizing.

decision.because: Column width is already core's business — six width words live there — so a seventh behaviour beside them is one place to change, not N.
